items.title: The Craft of Community-Engaged Teaching and Learning
items.notes: For CEL Reading Group, Lawrence University, 2026-2027

items.title: The Art of Memory
items.notes: Where memory palaces come from.

items.title: An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers
What Is the Name of This Book?
The Dawning of the Age of Stochasticity
items.description: Mumford argues that probability and statistics should move to the foundations of mathematics, and that thinking stochastically will reshape analysis, geometry, and the study of thought itself.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: the PDF on Mumford's own site.

items.title: Numbers and the World
items.subtitle: Essays on Math and Beyond
items.description: Essays on mathematics and beyond, many grown from Mumford's blog: on probability, pattern theory, physics, the brain, and what mathematics is.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online. Some of the blog posts it grew from are on Mumford's site (dam.brown.edu/people/mumford/blog).

items.title: On Proof and Progress in Mathematics
items.container: Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society 30 (1994), 161–177
items.description: Thurston's answer to the question of what mathematicians actually produce: not just theorems, but human understanding, passed between people by many more channels than formal proof.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: arXiv math/9404236.

items.title: The Skeleton Key of Mathematics
items.subtitle: A Simple Account of Complex Algebraic Theories
items.description: A short reference account of the algebraic ideas that unlock the rest: number systems, groups, fields, matrices, invariants, and quaternions, written for the general reader. (Dudley Ernest Littlewood, not his Cambridge namesake J. E.)
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: A Mathematician's Apology
items.description: Hardy's defence of pure mathematics as an art, written near the end of his career: beauty, seriousness, permanence, and his famous claim that real mathematics has no use.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: the University of Alberta's annotated electronic edition on the Internet Archive (public domain in Canada).

items.title: A Mathematician's Lament
items.container: Circulated as an essay; published by Keith Devlin in Devlin's Angle (MAA), March 2008; expanded as a book (Bellevue Literary Press, 2009)
items.description: Lockhart imagines music taught only as notation drills, then shows that this is how school teaches mathematics. A case for mathematics as an art of play, wonder, and argument.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: the essay, on Keith Devlin's site. The 2009 book is a library entry only.

items.title: The Method of Coordinates
items.description: Coordinates on a line, the plane, and space, then into four dimensions: how to see a 4-cube by its coordinates.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Part of the Gelfand Correspondence Program in Mathematics, whose booklets were mailed to students across the Soviet Union and later the United States. No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: Functions and Graphs
items.description: Drawing graphs by thought rather than by plotting points: linear, quadratic, and fractional-linear functions, and how graphs move.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Part of the Gelfand Correspondence Program in Mathematics, whose booklets were mailed to students across the Soviet Union and later the United States. No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: Sequences, Combinations, Limits
items.description: Problems on induction, finite differences, combinatorics, and limits, written for the correspondence school's students.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Part of the Gelfand Correspondence Program in Mathematics, whose booklets were mailed to students across the Soviet Union and later the United States. No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: Algebra
items.description: School algebra as a mathematician sees it, from the arithmetic of polynomials to inequalities, built from problems.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Part of the Gelfand Correspondence Program in Mathematics, whose booklets were mailed to students across the Soviet Union and later the United States. No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: Trigonometry
items.description: Trigonometry from its geometric roots, with the problems that make the identities inevitable rather than memorized.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Part of the Gelfand Correspondence Program in Mathematics, whose booklets were mailed to students across the Soviet Union and later the United States. No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: Geometry
items.description: The last book of the program: geometry through transformations, coordinates, and problems.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Part of the Gelfand Correspondence Program in Mathematics, whose booklets were mailed to students across the Soviet Union and later the United States. No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Mathematics in the Natural Sciences
items.container: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 13 (1960)
items.description: Why should mathematics invented for its own sake describe the physical world so well? Wigner calls it a gift we neither understand nor deserve.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: follow the link.

items.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Mathematics
items.description: Hamming's engineer's reply to Wigner: some of the effectiveness comes from what we choose to see, how we select our mathematics, and the questions we ask.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: follow the link.

items.title: Mathematical Problems
items.container: Bulletin of the AMS 8 (1902), trans. Mary Winston Newson; reprinted in Bull. AMS 37 (2000)
items.description: The Paris lecture that set out twenty-three problems for the new century, and why problems are the life of a subject.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: follow the link.

items.title: Science and Hypothesis
items.description: Poincaré on what is convention, what is experiment, and what is intuition, in number, magnitude, space, and force.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: Project Gutenberg. His Science and Method, with the essay on mathematical creation, is in The Foundations of Science (Gutenberg 39713).

items.title: Ten Lessons I Wish I Had Been Taught
items.description: Rota's advice from a career: on lecturing, on writing expository papers, on being remembered for one's expositions, and on the Feynman method.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: follow the link.

items.title: The Two Cultures of Mathematics
items.description: Theory builders and problem solvers: Gowers defends combinatorics by showing that its general principles are organized differently, not absent.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: follow the link.

items.title: What Is Good Mathematics?
items.description: Tao lists the many kinds of mathematical quality, from rigour to beauty to usefulness, and follows Szemerédi's theorem to show how they reinforce each other.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: follow the link.

items.title: Mathematical Education
items.description: Thurston on teaching: mathematics is not a ladder of skills but a tree with many ways up, and understanding grows by compression.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: follow the link.

items.title: On Teaching Mathematics
items.container: Address in Paris, 1997; trans. A. V. Goryunov
items.description: Arnold's polemic, from the Palais de la Découverte: mathematics is the part of physics where experiments are cheap, and axiomatic teaching kills it.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: follow the link.

items.title: Flatland
items.subtitle: A Romance of Many Dimensions
items.description: A square in a world of two dimensions meets a sphere, and learns to imagine a dimension he cannot see. The house's 4D experiments start here.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: follow the link.

items.title: Essays on the Theory of Numbers
items.description: Continuity and Irrational Numbers (the cuts), and The Nature and Meaning of Numbers: what numbers are, built from nothing but sets and maps.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: follow the link.

items.title: Introduction to Mathematical Philosophy
items.description: Russell's own plain account of the logic in Principia: number, order, infinity, descriptions, and classes, written in prison.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: Free to read online: follow the link.

items.title: How to Solve It
items.subtitle: A New Aspect of Mathematical Method
items.description: A method for problems: understand, plan, carry out, look back, with a dictionary of heuristics.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: What Is Mathematics?
items.subtitle: An Elementary Approach to Ideas and Methods
items.description: A grand tour of ideas and methods, from number theory to topology and the calculus of variations, with soap films.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: Geometry and the Imagination
items.description: Anschauliche Geometrie: geometry seen rather than proved, from lattices to configurations to the topology of surfaces.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: The Enjoyment of Mathematics
items.subtitle: Selections from Mathematics for the Amateur
items.description: Twenty-eight short pieces of mathematics chosen for pleasure, each complete in itself.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: A Mathematician's Miscellany
items.description: Littlewood's own collection of problems, jokes, cautionary tales, and reminiscences of Hardy and Ramanujan.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: The Psychology of Invention in the Mathematical Field
items.description: How mathematicians discover: Poincaré's omnibus, the unconscious, and a survey of how working mathematicians think (Einstein's answer included).
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: Proofs and Refutations
items.subtitle: The Logic of Mathematical Discovery
items.description: A classroom dialogue on Euler's formula V − E + F = 2, its counterexamples, and how proofs and definitions evolve together.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: The Mathematical Experience
items.description: What mathematics is like from the inside, from the ideal mathematician to the philosophy of the working mathematician.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: Mathematics for Human Flourishing
items.description: Mathematics as a human practice that meets basic desires: play, beauty, truth, justice, love, with letters from a prisoner learning mathematics.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: Measurement
items.description: Lockhart's own answer to his lament: a book of mathematics as art, on shape and motion, written as an invitation to work things out.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: Mathematics: A Very Short Introduction
items.description: Abstraction, proof, limits, dimension, and estimates, in a little over a hundred pages.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online; a library entry only.

items.title: Symmetry
items.description: Weyl's last book: bilateral, translational, rotational, and ornamental symmetry, and the groups behind them.
items.location: The Archive: the shelf of expositions
items.notes: No free copy online; a library entry only.
